# Sodium Meets Chlorine

<!-- STEP id="na" -->
## Sodium: One Valence Electron

Salt is made of sodium and chlorine, so we start with those two atoms. Sodium is 2,8,1. It has 1 valence electron in M, and just inside that is a full L-shell of 8.

<!-- STEP id="cl" -->
## Chlorine: One Short of an Octet

Chlorine is 2,8,7. It has 7 valence electrons in M, so it is 1 electron short of an octet.

<!-- STEP id="move" -->
## One Electron Moves

Move one electron from sodium to chlorine and count again. Sodium's outermost shell is now L, with 8 electrons, and chlorine's M-shell also has 8. If you move an electron the other way, neither atom has an octet.

**When salt forms, one electron moves from each sodium atom to a chlorine atom.**
